project.name: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
project.request: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

nodes.name: Punch Input Client
nodes.purpose: Reads punch key/click and movement input, plays local punch animation feedback, and requests a punch attempt from the server.

nodes.name: Punch Server
nodes.purpose: Authoritatively validates each punch attempt (distance to dummy, cooldown, alive character) and performs the strike-frame hit-detection check against the dummy.

nodes.name: Hit Counter State
nodes.purpose: Server-side per-player module storing hit count and cooldown timestamp, keyed by UserId; exposes increment/reset/cleanup operations.

nodes.name: Hit Reaction Service
nodes.purpose: On a confirmed hit, spawns the imported impact VFX at the contact point, plays the impact SFX, and triggers the dummy's brief flash/nudge reaction.

nodes.name: Training Dummy
nodes.purpose: Stationary, indestructible imported model providing the hitbox target and dummy geometry/reaction anchor; never takes damage or attacks.

nodes.name: Hit Counter HUD
nodes.purpose: Client-side HUD displaying the player's live hit count with a pop animation and a reset control, reading server-replicated counter state.

nodes.name: Respawn Handler
nodes.purpose: Rebinds humanoid/animator/root-part references for punch validation and animation playback when a player's character respawns, preserving session hit count.

edges.effect: Client fires a punch attempt request; server validates cooldown, distance and character state before proceeding.
Server tests overlap/raycast between the character's fist area and the dummy's hitbox during the strike frame.
On a valid hit, server instructs the per-player state module to increment that player's hit count and record cooldown.
Server notifies the reaction service to spawn VFX, play SFX, and nudge the dummy at the contact point.
Reaction service triggers the dummy's brief flash/nudge without altering its health or position permanently.
Server-side counter update replicates to the owning player's HUD, which increments the displayed number with a pop animation.
Player presses the reset control; client requests the server to zero that player's counter.
On respawn, respawn handler rebinds the player's humanoid/root-part references so punch validation continues to work against the new character instance.
Respawn handler ensures the existing per-player hit count in state is not reset or duplicated when the character respawns.

assetNeeds.role: Stationary, indestructible practice target providing the hitbox the player punches; user pre-approved this exact asset.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 1245720733 (creator Xtrah962). Inspect its embedded script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it does not deal damage, move, fight back, or knock itself down; must remain anchored/collidable and support a small nudge/flash reaction without falling over or being destroyed.

intent.experienceRole: This is the central object of the entire training loop: every punch, VFX burst, SFX cue and counter increment exists to register contact against this dummy, so its hitbox geometry and passive behavior directly gate whether the core loop functions.
intent.interaction: Non-attacking, non-moving prop: the player approaches and punches it; on a confirmed server-side hit it briefly flashes/nudges as feedback, then immediately returns to its resting stationary pose. It never damages the player or loses health itself.
reusableFeatures: Existing hitbox/collision geometry for hit-detection overlap
Any embedded idle/resting animation or physical joints usable for a brief nudge reaction
Embedded script behavior (scriptCount:1) that must be inspected for conflicting damage/AI logic before reuse

assetNeeds.role: Source of the R15 windup/strike/recovery punching animation clip played on the player's character when they throw a punch; user pre-approved this exact asset and clip.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 12061946559 (creator Auevi), embedded clip key 1/1/18/1. Inspect for R15 rig compatibility and for distinguishable windup, strike and recovery phases so the server can time the hit-detection check to the strike frame.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the visible, timed physical action of punching that the player's input maps to; without it the core loop has no observable attack animation and the strike-frame hit-detection timing has nothing to synchronize against.
intent.interaction: Plays fully on the player's character each time they press the punch input; the strike portion is the moment the server checks for a hit against the dummy. Animation completion (recovery) also gates the punch cooldown before another swing can be thrown.
reusableFeatures: Embedded R15 keyframe animation for windup/strike/recovery phases
Any embedded timing markers useful for aligning the strike frame with server hit-detection

assetNeeds.role: One-shot warm-accent impact burst VFX spawned at the fist-dummy contact point on each confirmed hit; user pre-approved this exact asset.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 86089736228455 (creator Spirit_Sage, 'Hit vfx m1 boxing'). Inspect particle emitters/attachments for one-shot burst behavior (not a continuous loop) and confirm color reads as a warm accent (orange/white spark or dust) consistent with the training theme.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers the primary visual reward feedback that sells a successful hit, reinforcing the 'practice and improve' satisfaction loop the theme calls for.
intent.interaction: Purely reactive/decorative feedback: it is spawned by the server-confirmed hit event at the contact point, plays a brief one-shot burst, and then cleans itself up; it does not accept player input.
reusableFeatures: Embedded ParticleEmitter/Attachment burst configuration
Existing color/size/lifetime tuning for a warm-accent spark or dust burst

assetNeeds.role: Sharp punch-impact sound cue played on each confirmed hit; user pre-approved this exact asset.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 132504023010884 (creator NickySergal, 'Punch Impact 1'). Must pass load and playback verification through the audio pipeline before acceptance; no substitute or generated sound is permitted if this fails.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the tactile 'thwack' audio feedback that, together with the VFX and dummy reaction, sells the weight and satisfaction of a landed punch as called for by the training theme.
intent.interaction: Triggered automatically by the server-confirmed hit event; plays once per hit synchronized with the VFX burst and counter increment. Not directly player-controlled beyond throwing the punch that causes it.
reusableFeatures: Existing mixed/mastered impact sound cue ready for direct playback via Sound/AudioPlayer

spec.assetStrategy: The user has already approved four specific Marketplace assets covering the bulk of requested behavior and media: (1) a Training Dummy model as the stationary practice target, (2) an R15 Punching Animations pack with a specific embedded clip for the windup/strike/recovery punch, (3) a Punch Impact SFX cue, and (4) a Hit VFX (boxing impact) model. Each must go through discovery/import/verification (Takko) before integration: inspect the dummy's existing script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it doesn't fight back, damage the player, or move on its own before reuse; inspect the animation model's embedded clip (key 1/1/18/1) for R15 compatibility and windup/strike/recovery timing; verify the SFX loads and plays through the audio pipeline; inspect the VFX model's particle/attachment rig for one-shot burst emission suitable for warm-accent impact feedback. Only the missing integration is authored: server-authoritative punch validation (cooldown, distance, hit window) and per-player hit-count state, since none of the four assets provide multiplayer-safe server logic; a reaction/feedback service that triggers the verified VFX/SFX/dummy nudge on a confirmed hit; and a HUD that displays/reset the counter with a pop animation, since no asset supplies UI. If inspection of the dummy's embedded script reveals damage/knockdown/AI behavior that conflicts with the 'stationary, indestructible' requirement, or if the animation clip is not R15-compatible or lacks distinct windup/strike/recovery phases, or if the SFX/VFX fail pipeline verification, these are reported as blocked gaps rather than silently replaced with procedural substitutes.
spec.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
spec.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
spec.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Player controls a single fighter who can move around and throw a punch at a stationary training dummy; approaching, punching and landing hits forms the entire playable loop.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: From spawn, the player can walk toward the dummy and trigger a punch that can land on it, with no win/lose condition or opponent AI required.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.description: A compact, single-room gym/dojo space with a flat floor, the dummy fixed at a central point, and the player spawning a few paces in front of it with open space to reposition; no additional rooms, hazards or obstacles.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one enclosed/open training room with a walkable floor, a centrally fixed dummy, and a collidable spawn point a short distance in front of it, with no additional gameplay areas.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch attempt (range to dummy, cooldown state, character alive) and performs the authoritative hit-detection check; client input and reported hits are never trusted directly.
requirements.acceptance: A modified or spoofed client punch/hit request that violates range, cooldown or animation-lock rules is rejected server-side and does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: Each player's hit count and punch cooldown state are stored server-side, keyed by player/UserId, updated on confirmed hits, zeroed on reset requests, and cleaned up when the player leaves.
requirements.acceptance: Server-side state exists per connected player, updates only in response to that player's confirmed hits/reset requests, and is removed without error when the player leaves the game.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.
requirements.acceptance: After a manual respawn, the player can still punch and register hits, the HUD shows the same session hit count as before respawn, and no duplicate HUD or stale connections are created.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.
requirements.acceptance: With two or more players punching the same dummy, each player's own Hit Counter and cooldown update independently and a reset by one player does not change another player's counter.

requirements.description: The four user-approved Marketplace assets (Training Dummy model, R15 punching animation pack, punch impact SFX, punch impact VFX model) are discovered, imported, inspected and integrated, preserving their existing verified behavior/media rather than being replaced with procedural substitutes.
requirements.acceptance: Each of the four approved assets is present in the scene/asset pipeline in a form that passes inspection and native verification, and gameplay scripts reference these imported assets directly instead of placeholder geometry, animation or sound.

nodes.name: Punch Input Client
nodes.purpose: Reads punch key/click and movement input, plays local punch animation feedback, and requests a punch attempt from the server.

nodes.name: Punch Server
nodes.purpose: Authoritatively validates each punch attempt (distance to dummy, cooldown, alive character) and performs the strike-frame hit-detection check against the dummy.

nodes.name: Hit Counter State
nodes.purpose: Server-side per-player module storing hit count and cooldown timestamp, keyed by UserId; exposes increment/reset/cleanup operations.

nodes.name: Hit Reaction Service
nodes.purpose: On a confirmed hit, spawns the imported impact VFX at the contact point, plays the impact SFX, and triggers the dummy's brief flash/nudge reaction.

nodes.name: Training Dummy
nodes.purpose: Stationary, indestructible imported model providing the hitbox target and dummy geometry/reaction anchor; never takes damage or attacks.

nodes.name: Hit Counter HUD
nodes.purpose: Client-side HUD displaying the player's live hit count with a pop animation and a reset control, reading server-replicated counter state.

nodes.name: Respawn Handler
nodes.purpose: Rebinds humanoid/animator/root-part references for punch validation and animation playback when a player's character respawns, preserving session hit count.

plan.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
plan.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.

requirements.description: Player controls a single fighter who can move around and throw a punch at a stationary training dummy; approaching, punching and landing hits forms the entire playable loop.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: From spawn, the player can walk toward the dummy and trigger a punch that can land on it, with no win/lose condition or opponent AI required.

On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the reset control sets the displayed and server-tracked counter for that player back to 0 immediately.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one enclosed/open training room with a walkable floor, a centrally fixed dummy, and a collidable spawn point a short distance in front of it, with no additional gameplay areas.

plan.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
plan.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.

requirements.description: Player controls a single fighter who can move around and throw a punch at a stationary training dummy; approaching, punching and landing hits forms the entire playable loop.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.

The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: From spawn, the player can walk toward the dummy and trigger a punch that can land on it, with no win/lose condition or opponent AI required.

During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.

Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.

requirements.description: A compact, single-room gym/dojo space with a flat floor, the dummy fixed at a central point, and the player spawning a few paces in front of it with open space to reposition; no additional rooms, hazards or obstacles.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one enclosed/open training room with a walkable floor, a centrally fixed dummy, and a collidable spawn point a short distance in front of it, with no additional gameplay areas.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch attempt (range to dummy, cooldown state, character alive) and performs the authoritative hit-detection check; client input and reported hits are never trusted directly.
requirements.acceptance: A modified or spoofed client punch/hit request that violates range, cooldown or animation-lock rules is rejected server-side and does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: Each player's hit count and punch cooldown state are stored server-side, keyed by player/UserId, updated on confirmed hits, zeroed on reset requests, and cleaned up when the player leaves.
requirements.acceptance: Server-side state exists per connected player, updates only in response to that player's confirmed hits/reset requests, and is removed without error when the player leaves the game.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.
requirements.acceptance: After a manual respawn, the player can still punch and register hits, the HUD shows the same session hit count as before respawn, and no duplicate HUD or stale connections are created.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.
requirements.acceptance: With two or more players punching the same dummy, each player's own Hit Counter and cooldown update independently and a reset by one player does not change another player's counter.

requirements.description: The four user-approved Marketplace assets (Training Dummy model, R15 punching animation pack, punch impact SFX, punch impact VFX model) are discovered, imported, inspected and integrated, preserving their existing verified behavior/media rather than being replaced with procedural substitutes.
requirements.acceptance: Each of the four approved assets is present in the scene/asset pipeline in a form that passes inspection and native verification, and gameplay scripts reference these imported assets directly instead of placeholder geometry, animation or sound.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: The user has already approved four specific Marketplace assets covering the bulk of requested behavior and media: (1) a Training Dummy model as the stationary practice target, (2) an R15 Punching Animations pack with a specific embedded clip for the windup/strike/recovery punch, (3) a Punch Impact SFX cue, and (4) a Hit VFX (boxing impact) model. Each must go through discovery/import/verification (Takko) before integration: inspect the dummy's existing script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it doesn't fight back, damage the player, or move on its own before reuse; inspect the animation model's embedded clip (key 1/1/18/1) for R15 compatibility and windup/strike/recovery timing; verify the SFX loads and plays through the audio pipeline; inspect the VFX model's particle/attachment rig for one-shot burst emission suitable for warm-accent impact feedback. Only the missing integration is authored: server-authoritative punch validation (cooldown, distance, hit window) and per-player hit-count state, since none of the four assets provide multiplayer-safe server logic; a reaction/feedback service that triggers the verified VFX/SFX/dummy nudge on a confirmed hit; and a HUD that displays/reset the counter with a pop animation, since no asset supplies UI. If inspection of the dummy's embedded script reveals damage/knockdown/AI behavior that conflicts with the 'stationary, indestructible' requirement, or if the animation clip is not R15-compatible or lacks distinct windup/strike/recovery phases, or if the SFX/VFX fail pipeline verification, these are reported as blocked gaps rather than silently replaced with procedural substitutes.

userSources.text: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. hierarchy.rule: Manifest slash paths describe separate nested Instances. FindFirstChild and WaitForChild take ONE child name, never a slash path. Never create a Folder whose name combines namespace and /children. Script filenames lose .server.luau, .client.luau, .module.luau or .luau at runtime. runtimeReference.sceneProperties: Name and Parent come from the path: omit both from properties. BasePart uses Color (Color3 value), Size (Vector3), CFrame, Anchored and CanCollide; it has no Color3 or Scale property. Set a walkable ground surface and a collidable spawn. references.rule: Part0, Part1, PrimaryPart, Attachment0/1 and Adornee use {type:'Ref',path:'exact scene path'}, never strings or nested Instances. Null path clears a reference. All referenced nodes must be declared in this bundle or existing dependencies. References resolve after construction, so forward references work. Humanoid, Animator, AnimationController, Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint and Highlight are supported scene classes. Motor6D requires BasePart Part0/Part1 and CFrame C0/C1. Models containing a Humanoid need a connected, unanchored rig to move, not just disconnected decorative parts.

runtimeReference.animation: Resize individual Parts with Size, recolor with Color, and animate via TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(seconds), {Size=targetSize, Color=targetColor}). Models scale with ScaleTo(number) and move with PivotTo(CFrame). Do not invent Part.Scale. Keep a crop's bottom above its soil while changing height.
runtimeReference.interactions: ProximityPrompt.Triggered connects on the server and supplies player. Validate humanoid health, distance, rate limits, ownership and current state on the server. Do not trust client attributes or RemoteEvent payloads. Per-player state requires indexing by player/UserId, not just a shared object name; clean associated objects and connections when they leave.
runtimeReference.presentation: A ScreenGui belongs in PlayerGui at runtime; LocalScripts may create it there. Put GUI Frames inside a ScreenGui, not directly inside PlayerGui. For a ResetOnSpawn=false HUD, keep its controller in StarterPlayerScripts or inside that persistent ScreenGui. A LocalScript directly under a StarterGui Folder restarts after respawn and can create duplicate, stale HUDs. Rebind health subscriptions on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. Send initial state after the client is ready, or use replicated attributes/value objects that the HUD reads initially and observes for changes. A one-time FireClient during PlayerAdded can be missed.
runtimeReference.audio: Audio is Marketplace-only. Discover complete reusable components first, preserving included sound references and provenance; search separately for missing sounds. Audio must pass the asset pipeline's loading, playback and listening checks before acceptance. Built-in, generated, placeholder and procedural audio are not permitted fallbacks. If verified audio is unavailable, report the unmet requirement rather than silently substituting sound. Do not invent IDs or claim unperformed playback tests.
runtimeReference.verification: FindFirstChild absence is a failure when an object is required: assert its presence before checking behavior. Tests must not skip absent objects, compare fabricated state tables, or call nonexistent signal Fire methods. Keep tests out of the live player loop; use the protected review harness for acceptance tests. Report untestable interactions honestly.

spec.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
spec.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
spec.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.sourceQuote:

requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: During normal play near the dummy, the default third-person camera keeps both the player character and the dummy visible on screen.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.
